newsitem.title: NEPAL: Deuba re-appoints dissidents in Nepal cabinet.
newsitem.headline: Deuba re-appoints dissidents in Nepal cabinet.

text.p: Nepali Prime Minister Sher Bahadur Deuba on Wednesday appointed eight new ministers to his cabinet, including five former ministers who had resigned to support a no-confidence motion against him last month.
State-owned Radio Nepal quoted a royal palace communique as saying King Birendra had made the appointments on the recommendation of Deuba.
It said the king, Nepal's constitutional head, had appointed Kamal Thapa as minister for local development and Ram Krishna Acharya as minister for commerce with full cabinet rank.
Prem Bahadur Bhandari (agriculture) and Rajib Parajuli (local development) got the junior rank of ministers of state.
All four belong to the Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP), a key partner in Deuba's coalition, and had resigned to support the communist-backed no confidence motion.
Deuba's centre-right coalition narrowly survived the motion which was triggered by a split among junior partners in the alliance.

Deuba also appointed another dissident, Anis Ansari, as a junior labour minister. Ansari, who belongs to the Nepal Sadbhavana Party (NSP), another coalition partner, had also resigned in December but abstained from voting against Deuba.
He flew to Singapore when the vote was taken.
Deuba appointed Fateh Singh Tharu agriculture minister in place of Padma Sundar Lawati who resigned over a corruption charge in December. Tharu was minister for commerce.
Moti Prasad Pahadi, a junior minister, was promoted to the cabinet rank of forest minister, vacant since a minister died two months ago.

A communist deputy belonging to the Nepal Workers' and Peasants' Party (NWPP), Bhakta Bahadur Rokaya, was appointed minister of state for forest and soil conservation and Mirza Dilsad Beg, an RPP dissident, became assistant minister for science technology.
Naresh Bahadur Singh from Deuba's own Nepali Congress party was appointed assistant minister for women and social welfare.
The three-party coaliton has 47 ministers including 30 from Nepali Congress, 13 from RPP and two from NSP. The other two hold independent status in parliament.
